title: Thanksgiving: no trading today, a short day Friday
text: U.S. stock markets are closed today for Thanksgiving, so there is no opening bell to watch. Trading comes back Friday morning, but stocks close early at 1 p.m. Eastern time. Short days often have fewer buyers and sellers, so prices can jump around more than usual. The prices on this page are from Wednesday's close. That day SPY, the S&P 500 fund, ended down 0.29% and QQQ, the Nasdaq 100 fund, ended down 0.65%. Both were much lower earlier in the day before they climbed back. Things to watch Friday: whether AI chip stocks keep falling, and what the coming Fed decision in December could mean for interest rates.

title: A wild ride on Wednesday
text: At its lowest point on Wednesday, the Nasdaq Composite was down about 4.6%. By the end of the day it was down only 0.62%. The S&P 500 finished down 0.25% and the Dow finished up 0.33%. A big drop that mostly disappears by the close tells us investors are nervous but still willing to buy when prices fall. It does not tell us which way prices go next.

title: AI chip makers are still the weak spot
text: NVIDIA fell 3.9% on Wednesday and is now about 39% below its high of the past year. Vertiv, which makes power and cooling gear for data centers, is about 54% below its high. AMD is about 38% below and Broadcom about 39% below. These are the group with the highest risk scores on our list, between 6.0 and 8.2 out of 10. A falling price can mean a bargain, or it can mean the business outlook got worse. Only time and new reports will tell which one it is.

title: Interest rates are still the big story
text: The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, up from 4.09% a year earlier. That is the interest rate the U.S. government pays to borrow for 10 years. Inflation rose to 3.8% in October, and minutes from the Fed's last meeting showed most officials expect more rate hikes. Higher rates make safe bonds more attractive, which can pull money away from stocks, especially fast growing tech stocks.

title: Lesson 68: What is an intraday swing?
text: Intraday means during one trading day. An intraday swing is how far a price moves between its low and its high on that same day. On Wednesday, the Nasdaq was down about 4.6% at one point but ended down only 0.62%. If you only looked at the close, you would think it was a calm day. It was not. Big swings like this usually happen when people are worried and react fast to news. For long term investors, the lesson is simple: one scary hour is not a reason to panic. Decide your plan before the market opens, not in the middle of a drop.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices, 52 week ranges, beta and company size come from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) as of Wednesday's close, the last trading day before Thanksgiving. Analyst price targets and company ratios come from FMP for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace; the free plan does not include them for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly or Intuitive Surgical. Sector moves are for Nasdaq listed companies. The 10 year Treasury yield comes from Alpha Vantage as a monthly average. News comes from public sources listed with each story. Risk scores and price scenarios are simple math, not predictions. This page is for learning, not financial advice.
